_rule: ARC-05-S10's no-literal-names guard. Engine tooling reads names from the contract loader, never from a list of its own. These five places hold a name for a reason that survives the rule. Four are PROSE keyed by a name, iterating the contract for the data. The fifth is a HOMOGRAPH: a docs-checkout mode that happens to be spelled like a tool package and has nothing to do with one. Every entry names the file, the literal it excuses, and why. The ceiling is 5 — a sixth needs an argument, not an edit. The fifth was argued at ARC-03-S05 (2026-09-09) and is the only entry of its kind; another homograph should be answered by renaming, not by a sixth row.

allow.reason: The `Use it when…` column: advice about when to choose a preset, which no amount of flag data implies. The rows come from contract.presets; a preset with no entry renders an empty cell rather than a wrong one, and the coverage assertion below notices.
The same advice column in the long-form document. Same shape, same reason.
The short preset gloss in the always-loaded rule file — `read-only (none)`, `full (all six)`. Prose, keyed by name; the names iterated are the contract's.

The `Also reported by` rule: the doctor checks PATH for the SDK, so this one code is reported by the doctor while the rest of its family is not. A structural signal would be a guess; the exception is one line and says which code and why.

A HOMOGRAPH, not a contract name. `MODE.full` is how much of the ServiceNow docs corpus is on disk — the opposite of a sparse checkout — and has no relationship to the `full` tool package, which is about which MCP tools a preset exposes. The story fixes the CLI as `--mode sparse|full` and ARC-06's launchers depend on that spelling, so it cannot be renamed away. Written once, in one frozen constant the module compares against; the four call sites hold no literal.
